n: Four documents, all dated Wednesday. The first is from Anthropic, the company that makes the Claude models. It says the company priced its initial public offering at $83.00 a share, that the offering is 980,000,000 shares, that trading is expected to begin Thursday on the Nasdaq, and that the offering is expected to close Friday. The other three are from GitHub's changelog. One makes team customizations generally available: a team can set shared plugins for its coding assistant as defaults, and the page says company policies still take precedence over team choices. One adds eight more services the assistant can connect to, in public preview. One says free security risk assessments now run automatically for organizations on its Team plan, to find exposed credentials and code vulnerabilities. What it means for your work: a company whose shares trade in public has to file regular reports that anyone can read, on its money, its risks and its plans. If your work depends on an AI tool, those filings become one more plain source on the company behind it. This note reports what the documents say and is not advice about buying or selling anything.
